findings.text: non-blocking: test_the_command_the_service_runs_carries_the_scheduled_retirement invokes the real `agent ingest --once` command without isolating HOME or overriding watch_publish.DEFAULT_OUTPUT, so its first tick now publishes through watch_publish.one_iteration to Path.home()/"public"/"imas-ambix"/"watch.json". Under a real HOME this test crosses the published artifact that lane readers consume, writing production output as a side effect of the suite. Reachable because of this node's change (the first tick publishes immediately); the file is outside this node's declared write paths and the worker recorded it under follow_ons, and the node's own gate ran with HOME and TMPDIR pointed at /tmp/reckon-crew-scratch/.../watch-gate-ROj4, so the recorded 46-passed result is not affected.

non-blocking: the cadence gate reads `last_published is None or _publication_clock() - last_published >= publish_every`, and _mark_published is called only through one_iteration's on_success, so last_published stays None until a publication actually succeeds. A persistently failing publication is therefore retried on the very next ingest tick (default 60 s) instead of at publish_every (default 300 s), multiplying the expensive watch_document derivation by roughly five under fault -- in the opposite direction to the plan's stated purpose of moving that cost off the ingest. The done-when frames the trigger as "since the last successful publication", so a retry-next-tick reading is defensible; recorded because a sustained fault is exactly when the cadence matters and nothing in the change bounds it.
